claims.evidence: NHS page for adults 19 to 64: at least 150 minutes moderate or 75 minutes vigorous a week, strengthening on at least 2 days.
Same NHS page, 150 moderate or 75 vigorous minutes a week.
NHS page: strengthening of all major muscle groups on at least 2 days; strength time does not count toward moderate aerobic minutes, so is done in addition to the 150 minutes.
NHS page talk test: moderate = can talk but not sing; vigorous = struggling to say more than a few words without pausing for breath.

NHS page advises reducing sitting and breaking up long inactive periods. NHS England Digital says the 2019 UK guidelines dropped the 10-minute criterion; the gov.uk update report says the 10-minute bout recommendation was removed as no longer necessary.
NHS page: at least 150 minutes moderate or 75 minutes vigorous a week for adults aged 19 to 64.
NHS inform: 150 moderate or 75 vigorous, 'or a combination of the two'; gov.uk CMO guidance also allows a combination of intensities.
NHS page: 75 minutes of vigorous activity can give similar health benefits to 150 minutes of moderate activity.
NHS page: activity every day, spread over several days; NHS inform: adults should aim to be active every day.
NHS page: moderate intensity if you can still talk but not sing.

Brisk walking and cycling shown on the NHS adult page; water aerobics, dancing, doubles tennis, pushing a lawn mower and hiking were returned together in NHS-affiliated lists (summary blended pages; moderately weak attribution for the less common examples).
NHS page: vigorous intensity leaves you struggling to say more than a few words without pausing for breath (breathing hard and fast).

NHS page gives running and swimming; skipping and aerobics appeared in NHS-affiliated vigorous lists; team sports and fast or uphill cycling not separately seen in this pass but consistent with the first-pass note.
gov.uk CMO guidelines: shorter durations of very vigorous activity, such as sprinting or stair climbing, as an alternative or in combination with other intensities.
NHS page: strengthening activities working all the major muscle groups on at least 2 days a week.
Lifting weights, push-ups, sit-ups, heavy digging, yoga, pilates and tai chi appeared in NHS-affiliated strength lists.
NHS: time spent on strength exercises does not count towards moderate aerobic activity; strength work is done in addition to the 150 minutes.
CMO guidance: muscle-strengthening at least two days a week, and any strengthening activity is better than none.
NHS: reduce time sitting and break up long inactive periods with light activity where possible.
CMO guidance: minimise sedentary time and, when physically possible, break up long periods of inactivity with at least light physical activity.
NHS adult page, returned in a search: 'Exercise just once or twice a week can reduce the risk of heart disease or stroke.'

Update report/NHS England Digital: the previous recommendation that activity count only in bouts of 10 minutes or more was removed in the 2019 guidelines. NHS inform does not mention bout length, so cite gov.uk or NHS England Digital rather than NHS inform.

NHS England Digital quoting the 2019 UK guidelines: no minimum amount of physical activity is required to achieve some health benefits. Attribution to 'the guidance' (UK CMOs) is right; the NHS page itself was not shown carrying it.
NHS Benefits of exercise: lowers risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes, depression, dementia (also falls in older adults, some cancers).
NHS Benefits of exercise: can boost self-esteem, mood, sleep quality and energy.
NHS older adults page: people aged 65 and over should be physically active every day, even if it is just light activity.

Strength, balance and flexibility on at least 2 days a week confirmed on the NHS older adults page; 150 minutes moderate (or 75 vigorous) confirmed by NHS inform. 'Built up gradually from current levels' was not shown in any returned text.
claims.newSentence: It recommends activities that improve strength, balance and flexibility on at least two days a week, and 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity a week.

claims.evidence: NHS adult page and older adults page: speak to a GP first if you have not exercised for some time or have a medical condition.

notes: Searches blend pages, so a few example lists (c11, c13, c16) rest on consistent NHS-affiliated lists rather than a single quoted page. One search result mentioned UK CMOs refreshing the guidelines in July 2026 and finding the recommended levels unchanged; the author should check that '2019 revision' wording and the numbers still match the current gov.uk page. c05/c22: cite gov.uk or NHS England Digital for the bouts point, not NHS inform. No second-person commands or unrouted urgency statements found.
